title: Integrating Prefetcher Selection with Dynamic Request Allocation Improves Prefetching Efficiency
problem: Hybrid hardware prefetchers sharing the same MSHRs and bandwidth resources create conflicts where competing prefetch requests from different algorithms negate each other's coverage, and existing prefetcher selection algorithms use inaccurate demand request allocation and coarse-grained selection criteria.
motivation: Commercial processors deploy multiple concurrent prefetching algorithms to cover diverse access patterns, but resource conflicts and poor coordination between prefetchers degrade overall effectiveness, especially for memory-intensive workloads.
method: Alecto decides, for each memory access the CPU actually needs, which prefetcher should attempt to fetch that data ahead of time. It evaluates which prefetcher can predict the access most correctly (accuracy), catch all the data the CPU will need (coverage), and deliver it with the right timing (timeliness). Rather than having all prefetchers speculate on every access, it routes each access only to the most suitable prefetcher for that pattern. This focused routing prevents prefetchers from polluting their lookup tables with bad patterns and stops them from wasting bandwidth and memory request slots by competing with each other.
key_novelty: Instead of using all prefetchers for every memory access, Alecto selects the best prefetcher for each individual access, improving accuracy, coverage, and timeliness while reducing energy waste from unnecessary training.
contributions: Identification that inaccurate demand request allocation and coarse-grained selection are the two key limitations of prior prefetcher selection approaches
Alecto algorithm that performs fine-grained, per-demand-request prefetcher selection and allocation
2.76% single-core and 7.56% eight-core IPC improvement over state-of-the-art RL-based Bandit selection; 5.25% gain on memory-intensive benchmarks
48% reduction in prefetcher table access energy (7% reduction on full memory hierarchy) with less than 1 KB storage overhead

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 48% prefetcher table energy reduction; 7% full memory hierarchy energy reduction

limitations: Evaluation focuses on CPU memory hierarchies; applicability to GPU or accelerator memory subsystems with different access pattern characteristics is not discussed.
primary_theme: fine-grained per-request prefetcher selection to reduce hybrid prefetcher conflicts
